adds.title: LGBT rights in South Africa - Wikipedia
adds.summary: The national dossier this Free State record is assessed under: the 1996 Constitution was the world's first to expressly bar sexual-orientation discrimination, the Constitutional Court's December 2005 judgment pushed Parliament to legalise same-sex marriage (Civil Union Act, National Assembly vote 229-41, November 2006), and the Alteration of Sex Description and Sex Status Act 2003 allows a person to change sex status in the population registry - and therefore on identity documents and passports - on proof of medical treatment such as hormone therapy, without requiring surgery. The page adds that gender-affirming care is concentrated in the main cities, so transgender people in provinces like the Free State 'must travel long distances to major cities' to reach it, with private treatment costing hundreds of thousands of rands and long public waiting lists, and records the Justice Department's National Task Team (2011) and 2014 National Intervention Strategy for LGBTI Communities aimed at hate crimes against LGBT people. This grounds the record's at-national-score assessment in the concrete national framework a Free State visitor stands under, since no Free State-specific trans source was surfaced.

adds.title: LGBT rights in France - Wikipedia
adds.summary: The national framework this Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes record stands under: France legalised same-sex marriage and full adoption in 2013 (civil solidarity pacts since 1999), Penal Code article 225-1 has covered 'gender identity' since an 18 November 2016 amendment that replaced 'sexual identity' (protected since 2012), and homophobic hate speech has carried penalties up to EUR 45,000 and/or one year's imprisonment since a 31 December 2004 amendment. On legal gender recognition, a bill approved by the Senate on 6 November 2015 and by the National Assembly on 24 May 2016 was signed into law on 18 November 2016 and took effect on 1 January 2017: it abolished the sex-reassignment-surgery and forced-sterilisation requirements, rejected a Senate amendment that would have demanded proof of medical treatment, and requires going before a court rather than any medical intervention; transsexualism is classed under long-term-illness ALD 31, so gender-affirming treatment is funded by the Sécurité Sociale. It supplies the concrete national rules on documents, protection and care that a trans visitor to Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes encounters and grounds the record's at-national-score assessment, since the region's own page carries no trans-specific content.
